newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti aims for beak-even in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti aims for beak-even in 1997.

text.p: Italy's information technology company Olivetti is working to get as close to breakeven as it can for 1997, sources at the company comfirmed on Wednesday.

The group's chief executive Roberto Colaninno was reported to have told union leaders late Tuesday that the company was working towards break-even this year after a meeting between Olivetti's top management, union leaders and the Minister of Labour Pierluigi Bersani.
The company source confirmed that Olivetti was working to get as close as it could to break-even for 1997, excluding its interest in mobile phone group Omnitel.
The source also said that the company's performance in 1997 was going according to the group's budget, and Olivetti planned 300 billion lire of investment in 1997 (excluding Omnitel).
Olivetti made a pretax loss of 800 billion lire in 1996, and has not made a profit since 1990.
